meaning: Completeness in revelation and divine communication
description: In Jewish tradition, the number 27 holds significance because the Hebrew alphabet, including the five sofit letters (final forms), totals 27 characters, linking the number to the completeness of written revelation and God's word. As the cube of 3 (3×3×3), it intensifies the symbolism of the number three regarding divine perfection and wholeness, raised to its highest power. In Christian tradition, this symbolism is further strengthened as the trinitarian meaning of the number three—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—is elevated to the third power, and because the New Testament consists of exactly 27 books. Overall, the number 27 points to the complete and full delivery of God's revelation, both through the building blocks of language and the canon of Scripture.

footnotes.text: The five sofit letters (כ→ך, מ→ם, נ→ן, פ→ף, צ→ץ) are special final forms used when a letter appears at the end of a word. The fact that these bring the total number of characters to 27 is attributed symbolic significance in Kabbalistic tradition, where the five final forms are linked to five levels of divine severity (gevurot).

The canon of the New Testament with 27 books was formally confirmed at the councils of Hippo (393 AD) and Carthage (397 AD), although the list was in use already from Athanasius's Easter letter in 367 AD.

In rabbinic tradition, the total number of letters in the alphabet is discussed in the Talmud (Shabbat 104a), where the five final forms are attributed to the prophets, reinforcing the connection between the 27 characters and prophetic revelation.
